headline: A wildcard name in a certificate is held to an excluded name constraint it can reach.
summary: A dNSName excluded subtree names what a certificate may not present. A wildcard subject alternative name is not one name but every name one label below its parent, and it was compared as though it were a single literal string, so an exclusion of bar.example.com admitted a certificate whose only name was *.example.com. That certificate presents bar.example.com. The comparison now asks whether a wildcard reaches into an excluded subtree, and refuses it when it does.

Security: pki.path.validate refuses a certificate whose wildcard dNSName reaches a name an excluded subtree forbids. An excluded subtree states the names a certificate must not present, and a wildcard subject alternative name stands for every name one label below its parent rather than for the literal text. Comparing the text alone let a leaf carrying only *.example.com pass an exclusion of bar.example.com, which is a name that leaf presents. Any chain whose certificate authority relies on an excluded dNSName subtree to keep a subordinate away from a name was affected, in every version that shipped name-constraint validation. The permitted direction is unchanged and is not widened by this: a permitted subtree still has to cover the whole of a wildcard, so a base of foo.com admits *.foo.com while a base of bar.example.com does not admit *.example.com. A wildcard reaches exactly one label, so an excluded name deeper than that is out of its reach and is not refused: *.example.com is still admitted against an exclusion of deep.bar.example.com.
